question.problem:
The matrices $A$ and $B$ are given below. Given that $A$ is row equivalent to $B$, then find a basis of $\text{Null}(A).$

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 \\ 2 & -5 & 2 \\ 1 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$
question.worked_solution:
To find a basis of $\text{Null}(A),$ we need to solve the equation $Ax=0$ and express the solution as a linear combination of linearly independent vectors. Those vectors form a basis of $\text{Null}(A).$

Since $A∼B,$ the equation $Ax=0$ is equivalent to the equation $Bx=0,$ which corresponds to the following system:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+{x}_{3}=0 \\ {x}_{2}=0\end{aligned}
$$

So, the general solution is ${x}_{1}=-{x}_{3}$ and ${x}_{2}=0,$ where ${x}_{3}$ is a free variable. Therefore, if $x\in \text{Null}(A),$ then

$$
[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-{x}_{3} \\ 0 \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}]={x}_{3}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{3}\in R.
$$

This implies that 

$$
B=\{[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\}
$$

is a basis of $\text{Null}(A)$ since it is a linearly independent set and its vectors generate $\text{Null}(A).$
